Marissa / Lauren —

Draft summary below (I kept it short so it fits the one-pager):

Redwood TIA summary (pilot-level) — draft bullets:
1) Routing & residency: Tenant-level routing policy pins request processing to eu-west-2 for Olive's UK pilot. No production KV caches will be populated in other regions for pinned tenants; ephemeral caches are cleared on session termination.
2) Logging & escrow snapshot: We can export encrypted request logs (TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest) on a weekly schedule to a customer-owned UK bucket or our Redundancy vault in eu-west-2. Snapshot includes request id, timestamp, model id, and metadata; bodies can be redacted on request. Snapshots are checksummed (SHA-256) and shared via secure link.
3) Subprocessor controls & attenuation: Current hosted subprocessors that may process traffic outside region are: FastCache Inc. (edge caching), TelemetryAnalytics Ltd. (aggregated metrics). For pilot we propose: (a) lock to a named subprocessor set, (b) 30-day notification on any subprocessor addition/change, (c) ability to opt for a 7-day rollback to prior routing policy if a change materially affects residency.
4) When to escalate to DTIA: If the customer requires contractual commitments beyond SCCs/UK IDTA (e.g., contractual guarantees on processor hosting locations or independent attestations on subprocessor routing), we recommend a scoped DTIA; otherwise the TIA summary + SCCs/IDTA is generally sufficient for short pilots.

I'll attach this as a PDF and include the subprocessor CSV. Note: legal should review the rollback SLA language if Olive wants an automated technical rollback rather than a contractual remedy.
